newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba to mass produce smallest 64MB DRAM chips.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba to mass produce smallest 64MB DRAM chips.

text.p: Toshiba Corp said on Thursday that it plans to start mass-producing the world's smallest 64-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chip from the fourth quarter of this year.
Initial production of the 79.4 square mm chips, which Toshiba said are also the world's fastest, will be 500,000 units a month, Toshiba said in a statement.
Toshiba said it would start sample shipments in July.

Toshiba expects output of 64-megabit DRAM chips, including the smallest chips, to total about one million chips a month during the six months to December 31, 1997, rising to three million units per month by the end of March 1998, a company spokesman said.

The company sees output of 16-megabit DRAM chips staying at around seven million units a month through the end of March 31, 1998, the spokesman said, but adding that this may change according to market demand.
